steps.t: Do any apt upgrades or driver updates now, not this week
steps.why: The team's pre-test document: updates "MUST be done DAYS in advance", because what they break is often inexplicable. pretest repo warns when either machine changed packages in the last 3 days.
steps.cmd: ./pretest repo --only R4

steps.t: Charge both battery housings
steps.why: Talos runs on two smart battery housings, port and starboard, ORed onto one bus. Each holds a MaxAmps 8000 mAh 5S2P LiPo, charged to at most 4.15 V a cell (20.75 V). On the bench Talos runs from a power supply, so the packs are only tested once they're in.

checklist.title: The day before, on the bench

steps.t: Inspect and clean the O-ring sealing surfaces (inside both lids)
steps.why: Dirt on a sealing surface is how water gets in. Check every time the hull is sealed.

steps.t: Bench-test every new or changed piece of software on the robot itself
steps.why: "Integration is hell": a new YOLO model is tested on the ZED and the Orin, not only on a laptop. This is the part that takes longest.

steps.t: Commit and push every submodule, then commit release with the new pins
steps.why: One release commit names the exact code that goes in the water. A pin that isn't pushed can't be checked out by anyone else, and can't be rolled back to.
steps.cmd:
cd ~/osu-uwrt/release
git submodule status            # '+' = checked out away from its pin
git add src/riptide_control     # each submodule you changed
git commit -m "Pre RPAC test 10-30-26"
git push

steps.t: Clean build on op-top
steps.why: colcon never removes a deleted package from install/, and stale build caches cause the "dumb compile errors" the document warns about.
steps.cmd:
cd ~/osu-uwrt/release
rm -rf build install log && colcon build

steps.t: Delete the Orin's workspace and deploy clean
steps.why: Forces a clean build on the Orin. Afterwards pretest repo compares every deployed file with release (an rsync dry run) and checks the build is newer than the sources.
steps.cmd:
source ~/osu-uwrt/riptide_setup/install/setup.bash
ssh ros@orin2 'rm -rf ~/colcon_deploy'
cd ~/osu-uwrt/release && colcon deploy orin2 --clean

steps.t: pretest repo: pins, pushed, robot runs this code, trees parse
steps.why: All PASS before you go on. R5 runs checkBT on every tree (it rewrites the files, so the tool restores them afterwards).
steps.cmd:
cd ~/osu-uwrt/release/pretest_checks
./pretest repo --with-tests

steps.t: Run the trees you'll run at the pool in Nereus, with the real detector
steps.why: Nereus renders the cameras and the stack's own YOLO detector runs on them, so a tree is tested end to end before it costs pool time. The tool's sim stage is planned, not built: run it by hand. Keep it off the robot's graph. A shell that sourced config_rmw.bash uses the team Zenoh config, which connects to orin2: with Talos powered on the LAN, the sim joins the real robot's ROS graph (its viewer, kill slot 1, MPC topics). Drop the team config as below in both terminals, or run it with Talos off or op-top off the robot LAN. The planned S0 check exists for this.
steps.cmd:
unset ZENOH_ROUTER_CONFIG_URI ZENOH_SESSION_CONFIG_URI   # both terminals: no team config
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd        # terminal 1
ros2 launch nereus sim.launch.py pool:=rpac active_control_model:=mpc mpc_model:=sim   # terminal 2

steps.t: pretest bench: boards, rates, kill, ESCs, controller, drift, TF, DVL, cameras
steps.why: Read-only, about five minutes, robot on the bench on a power supply. It starts the stopped bench launches (sensors and perception only) and runs the controller only under a held software kill.
steps.cmd: ./pretest bench

steps.t: Tare the gyro only if B10 warns, with Talos level and still
steps.why: A tare taken tilted or moving bakes an error into every heading. The tool reports the bias but never tares on its own.
steps.cmd: ros2 action send_goal /talos/gyro/tare riptide_msgs2/action/TareGyro "{num_samples: 100000, timeout_seconds: 20}"

steps.t: pretest guided: localization by hand, vision, AprilTag, thruster test, actuators
steps.why: A person at the robot, a second person at the kill switch, the Nereus viewer open. The thruster test (G4) is the only step that spins anything.
steps.cmd: ./pretest guided --apriltag --actuators torpedo,dropper

steps.t: Dry-run every procedure you plan for the pool (identification, a tune, a tree)
steps.why: "You should be 100% confident in your ability to perform all planned operations." Pool time spent learning a procedure is wasted.

steps.t: Changed anything? Commit, bump release, redeploy, rerun repo and bench
steps.why: G7 fails if the release checkout or the deployed code changed since G0. Never plan on git at the pool: fix it now.

steps.t: Depressurization test (PVT), then the green subconn cover on
steps.why: The hull is pumped down by hand (0.05 bar below ambient in the 2025 design report) and watched for at least 5 minutes. The green cover says Talos is sealed and tested. Open it again and the test has to be repeated.

steps.t: Tell the team nobody opens Talos or swaps parts until the test
steps.why: Any internal mechanical or electrical change voids the localization and thruster tests you just did.

steps.t: Pack everything on the pack list
Check the summary of the latest runs
steps.why: One line per stage with its latest result, so everyone can see what was tested and what was skipped.
steps.cmd: ./pretest summary

steps.t: Leave on time
steps.why: The release README's third pre-test step: "Leave for the pool on time. (no, really, try to leave on time)".

steps.t: Router, opbox and tether up; op-top on the robot LAN
steps.why: Everything talks over the team router (192.168.1.0/24). The tether joins Talos to it; the opbox gives the LAN internet and the time server.
steps.cmd:
ping -c 3 orin2
chronyc tracking        # op-top's clock against the opbox
refs: The robot LAN and the tether

steps.t: Kill switch OUT, then power Talos on
steps.why: With the switch out the thrusters have no power, whatever any software does. Talos boots killed, and the launcher service starts on its own.

steps.t: Launcher: load talos_launch_mpc.yaml, start the sensors, perception and autonomy
steps.why: Start hardware, navigation (riptide_hardware2's, the first of the two), zed, tensorrt, mapping and autonomy. Leave control_system for later. The diagnostics node is no longer used.
steps.cmd: http://orin2:8080

steps.t: Start the Nereus viewer against the robot
steps.why: The viewer is the operator UI. It kills Talos on slot 1 from the moment it opens, until someone presses Enable.
steps.cmd:
source ~/osu-uwrt/release/scripts/dds_scripts/config_rmw.bash   # Zenoh client of orin2
ros2 launch nereus robot.launch.py pool:=rpac

steps.t: Quick health check: boards, rails and battery bus, rates, kill, ESCs
steps.why: Catches what the drive over changed. pretest dayof is planned for this; until then, run the bench checks that don't start anything. In the viewer: the FOG temperature and the PORT and STBD charge.
steps.cmd: ./pretest bench --only B3,B4,B5,B6,B7 --power battery

steps.t: Hull opened or anything rewired since the bench? Rerun the thruster test on the stand
steps.why: Any internal change voids the bench's thruster test. Run it again before control_system starts (the two would both command the thrusters over CAN): killed first, then Enable, one full cycle, pull the switch, Ctrl-C. Talos on its stand, props clear, someone at the switch.
steps.cmd:
ssh ros@orin2
source ~/colcon_deploy/install/setup.bash
ros2 run riptide_controllers2 thruster_test_canbus

steps.t: Start control_system last, with Talos killed
steps.why: An enabled robot with the controller running spins its thrusters. Killed, the MPC publishes zero thrust.

steps.t: Name the kill-switch holder; switch out; two people lift Talos in
steps.why: Talos is about 32 kg dry. One person's only job is the switch: they hold it, and they pull it when anyone says so.

steps.t: Killed, Talos floats: rises slowly and settles at the surface
steps.why: The MPC model has Talos 1.63 N positive, just under RoboSub's minimum of 0.5 % of its mass (1.68 N); the untethered fit was right on it. A robot that sinks or hangs needs buoyancy added before flying; one that rises fast has changed since it was weighed.

steps.t: Switch in, Enable in the viewer, wait for the ESCs, Dive in place
steps.why: The ESC boards hold their motors for about 5 s after power comes back. Dive in place targets the current x, y and heading, level, at the configured depth.

steps.t: Small moves first: forward 0.5, turn 30, then hold and watch
steps.why: Type moves into the viewer's search (Ctrl+P). While it holds, plot the MPC's disturbance estimate: a large constant torque means the model's buoyancy or trim is off.
steps.cmd: plot disturbance        # Ctrl+P in the viewer: /talos/controller/mpc/disturbance

steps.t: Sensor sanity: DVL lock, depth, both cameras, detections, still pose
steps.why: Each fails in its own way in water: no bottom lock near the floor or a wall, depth offset, a fogged lens. Check them before blaming a tree.

steps.t: Put the course in the prior map, then calibrate on the AprilTag
steps.why: The trees navigate in the map frame. Edit the prior map in the viewer (Ctrl+M), deploy riptide_mapping2, then Calibrate in the Mapping panel with the tag in view.
steps.cmd:
cd ~/osu-uwrt/release && colcon deploy orin2 --packages-select riptide_mapping2
# then restart mapping in the launcher; Calibrate in the viewer's Mapping panel

steps.t: Start a bag before every run
steps.why: A run you didn't record can't be debugged at home. Record on the robot, so the bag survives the tether.

steps.t: Run trees: Enable, Start, unplug, insert the switch
steps.why: A tree waits for state/kill to go false, then 6 s more. Untethered, the physical switch is the only kill.

steps.t: Identification runs, untethered, from the committed model
steps.why: A tethered run fits the tether's pull as buoyancy. IdentificationTree first flies to the map origin facing map +x at 0.85 m, so map and calibrate first; leave 3 m clear ahead (map +x) and to port (map +y) of the origin, and 2.5 m below. Red breath right after the blue fast flash: pool_identify wasn't launched.
steps.cmd:
ssh ros@orin2
tmux new -s ident
source ~/colcon_deploy/install/setup.bash
source ~/uwrt_config/source/zenoh_server.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 launch riptide_mpc pool_identify.launch.py wait_for_trigger:=true max_iterations:=1

steps.t: Kill switch out, Talos out with two people, power off
steps.why: Out first: nobody's hands go near the thrusters while the robot can be enabled.

steps.t: Copy bags, SVOs and identification sessions off the Orin
steps.why: They live only on the robot until copied, and the next clean deploy or full disk is not a backup.
steps.cmd:
rsync -a ros@orin2:/home/ros/bags/ ~/bags/
rsync -a ros@orin2:/home/ros/osu-uwrt/mpc_identification/ ~/mpc_identification/

steps.t: Commit what changed at the pool, bump release
steps.why: Prior-map edits, tuned parameters and models are files on op-top or the Orin. Commit them in their submodules, then commit release with the new pins, so the next test starts from them.

steps.t: Tag release with the date and publish a GitHub release
steps.why: The README: tag with the date of the test and release it, with notes on what was tested, as a backup to roll back to.
steps.cmd:
cd ~/osu-uwrt/release
git tag 10-30-26-talos && git push origin 10-30-26-talos
gh release create 10-30-26-talos --title "Pool test 10-30-26" --notes-file notes.md

steps.t: Write it up: what was tested, what broke, where the data is
steps.why: The release notes are the team's record of the day. Bag and session paths make the data findable.
